content.comment_body: Hello, I have installed [product_name] software from DVD ([article_no], [version_no]) on a Windows 11 laptop. The controller is connected directly via Ethernet and a USB-Ethernet adapter. The controller uses [article_no] with [version_no] firmware. IP addresses are set up correctly and are static. The PC and controller can ping each other successfully. However, the software cannot establish a connection to the controller. Any assistance would be appreciated. Thank you, [user_name]
Have you checked if the relevant ports are open in your Windows firewall?
@ [user_name], Are both the USB Ethernet adapter and the [product_name] controller operating in the same IP subnet?

Hi @ [user_name], At this point, I believe this is likely the main cause of the issue. I've reviewed multiple PDF manuals, but haven't found the specific information. Which firewall ports need to be open to enable communication between these devices? @ [user_name], Both the PC and controller are assigned to the same subnet: PC 192.168.0.10, controller 192.168.0.25, within an isolated network containing only these devices. Both devices can ping each other. I think I'm close to resolving the issue. Thank you for the assistance, [user_name]
I'm not asking whether the PC and controller are in the same subnet—I'm asking if the USB Ethernet adapter and the controller share the same subnet.

Hello, The USB-Ethernet adapter and the controller are configured within the same subnet. The PC has no other network connections enabled (WiFi is off, and no additional wired Ethernet ports are available). There are no external network resources accessible—only the controller for programming.
Please specify the IP address of the USB Ethernet adapter and the controller, as well as their subnet mask.

The USB-Ethernet adapter on the PC uses IP 192.168.0.10 with a subnet mask of 255.255.255.0. There are no other network connections enabled on this PC. This setup is an isolated network with just two devices directly connected. The controller has IP 192.168.0.25 and subnet mask 255.255.255.0. Pinging between PC and controller works from both ends. It seems that the problem is due to the Windows 11 firewall settings on the host PC. Could you identify which network ports are required for communication between these devices, so I can ensure they are permitted through the firewall?
Please refer to the attached file.
Thank you for the provided link.

analysis.insight_summary: A user is having difficulties establishing communication between [product_name] software ([version_no]) and a [product_name] controller via Ethernet and USB-Ethernet adapter, even though both devices pass ping tests in an isolated Windows 11 network. The problem appears to be linked to either network configuration or firewall port settings. The community discussion includes clarifications about IP subnetting and requests for information regarding required firewall ports. The lack of clear documentation about necessary network ports for [company_name] products leads to user frustration and further queries.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects seamless communication between the [product_name] software and controller using a direct network setup. They also hope for clear, readily available documentation outlining firewall and port requirements for successful communication with [company_name] products.
